newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall as market waits for new cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall as market waits for new cabinet.

text.p: Thai stocks closed marginally lower on Monday on continued uncertainty about the shape of a new Thai cabinet being formed by coalition leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, brokers said.
The SET Index ended 2.53 points lower at 967.77 on moderate 5.5 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index fell 0.23 point to 74.37.

"Investors, especially foreigners, sold large capitalised stocks on market rumours that Amnuay Viravan won't be appointed finance minister in the new coalition government," said Sanpong Limthamrongkul of Jardine Fleming Thanakom Securities.
The composite index retreated in the afternoon from its intra-day peak of 981.68, or up 11.38 points, posted shortly after it opened in the morning.
Some brokers said the index declined on rumours that Amnuay, tipped earlier to take over the finance ministerial job, may be named only an economic advisor.
Chavalit's coalition partners have demanded to share key economic posts but none has announced it would seek Amnuay's expected job at the finance ministry.
The new cabinet line-up is expected to be announced later this week after Chavalit is appointed prime minister on Monday.
Big capitalised stocks hit by profit taking included Siam Cement which slipped four baht to 896, Avanced Info declined six to 314, and United Communication fell 12 to 208.
Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, falling one baht to 79, National Finance gained 1.50 to 66.50, and Bangkok Bank rose two to 210.
